verses.context: Facing enemies who wanted him dead, David opens this psalm by declaring where his confidence actually comes from.

KJV.text: Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord.
KJV.displayText: Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord.

BSB.text: Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!
BSB.displayText: Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!

CPDV.text: Wait for the Lord, act manfully; and let your heart be strengthened, and remain with the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: Wait for the Lord, act manfully; and let your heart be strengthened, and remain with the Lord.

verses.context: David closes this psalm about facing hostile enemies by telling his own heart to keep waiting and stay brave.

KJV.text: The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.
KJV.displayText: The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.

BSB.text: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song.

CPDV.text: The Lord is my helper and my protector. In him, my heart has hoped and I have been helped. And my flesh has flourished again. And from my will, I shall confess to him.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is my helper and my protector. In him, my heart has hoped and I have been helped. And my flesh has flourished again. And from my will, I shall confess to him.

verses.context: In a psalm asking God not to stay silent, David shifts partway through to thanking God for already helping him.

KJV.text: The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.
KJV.displayText: The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.

BSB.text: The LORD gives His people strength; the LORD blesses His people with peace.
BSB.displayText: The LORD gives His people strength; the LORD blesses His people with peace.

CPDV.text: The Lord will give virtue to his people. The Lord will bless his people in peace.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord will give virtue to his people. The Lord will bless his people in peace.

verses.context: This closes a psalm describing a violent storm as the voice of God, ending with a wish for peace over his people.

KJV.text: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
KJV.displayText: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.

BSB.text: For His anger is fleeting, but His favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
BSB.displayText: For His anger is fleeting, but His favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.

CPDV.text: For wrath is in his indignation, and life is in his will. Toward evening, weeping will linger, and toward morning, gladness.
CPDV.displayText: For wrath is in his indignation, and life is in his will. Toward evening, weeping will linger, and toward morning, gladness.

verses.context: Written for the dedication of his house, David's psalm turns from sorrow to joy within a single verse.

KJV.text: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye.
KJV.displayText: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye.

BSB.text: I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will give you counsel and watch over you.
BSB.displayText: I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will give you counsel and watch over you.

CPDV.text: I will give you understanding, and I will instruct you in this way, in which you will walk. I will fix my eyes upon you.
CPDV.displayText: I will give you understanding, and I will instruct you in this way, in which you will walk. I will fix my eyes upon you.

verses.context: After describing being forgiven, David reports God speaking directly to him, promising to guide and teach him.

KJV.text: O taste and see that the Lord is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
KJV.displayText: O taste and see that the Lord is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.

BSB.text: Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!
BSB.displayText: Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!

CPDV.text: Taste and see that the Lord is sweet. Blessed is the man who hopes in him.
CPDV.displayText: Taste and see that the Lord is sweet. Blessed is the man who hopes in him.

verses.context: Written after David pretended to be insane to escape a hostile king, this psalm invites the reader to test God's goodness personally.

KJV.text: The righteous cry, and the Lord heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
KJV.displayText: The righteous cry, and the Lord heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.

BSB.text: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears; He delivers them from all their troubles.
BSB.displayText: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears; He delivers them from all their troubles.

CPDV.text: The just cried out, and the Lord heard them, and he freed them from all their tribulations.
CPDV.displayText: The just cried out, and the Lord heard them, and he freed them from all their tribulations.

verses.context: The same psalm continues by describing God listening whenever people in trouble cry out for help.

KJV.text: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
KJV.displayText: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

BSB.text: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.

CPDV.text: The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.

verses.context: Right after that, the same psalm adds that God stays close to anyone who is brokenhearted or crushed in spirit.

KJV.text: Delight thyself also in the Lord; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
KJV.displayText: Delight thyself also in the Lord; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.

BSB.text: Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.
BSB.displayText: Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.

CPDV.text: Delight in the Lord, and he will grant to you the petitions of your heart.
CPDV.displayText: Delight in the Lord, and he will grant to you the petitions of your heart.

verses.context: Advising against envy toward people who do wrong, David offers this alternative instead: finding joy in God himself.

KJV.text: Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
KJV.displayText: Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.

BSB.text: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it.
BSB.displayText: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it.

CPDV.text: Reveal your way to the Lord, and hope in him, and he will accomplish it.
CPDV.displayText: Reveal your way to the Lord, and hope in him, and he will accomplish it.

verses.context: David goes on immediately to say that handing his plans over to God is what makes them succeed.

KJV.text: The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord: and he delighteth in his way.
KJV.displayText: The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord: and he delighteth in his way.

BSB.text: The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey.
BSB.displayText: The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey.

CPDV.text: The steps of a man will be directed by the Lord, and he will choose his way.
CPDV.displayText: The steps of a man will be directed by the Lord, and he will choose his way.

verses.context: By the end of this wisdom psalm, David describes a good life as something actively directed and steadied by God.

KJV.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
KJV.displayText: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.

BSB.text: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
BSB.displayText: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.

CPDV.text: My soul, why are you saddened? And why do you disquiet me? Hope in God, for I will still confess to him: the salvation of my countenance and my God.
CPDV.displayText: My soul, why are you saddened? And why do you disquiet me? Hope in God, for I will still confess to him: the salvation of my countenance and my God.

verses.context: Talking to his own discouraged heart, the psalm's writer repeats this line as a refrain to talk himself back into hope.

KJV.text: To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
KJV.displayText: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

BSB.text: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song. God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble.
BSB.displayText: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble.

CPDV.text: Our God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the tribulations that have greatly overwhelmed us.
CPDV.displayText: Our God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the tribulations that have greatly overwhelmed us.

verses.context: Written by the sons of Korah, a family of temple singers, this psalm opens by naming God as a safe place during disaster.

KJV.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
KJV.displayText: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

BSB.text: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”
BSB.displayText: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”

CPDV.text: Be empty, and see that I am God. I will be exalted among the peoples, and I will be exalted upon the earth.
CPDV.displayText: Be empty, and see that I am God. I will be exalted among the peoples, and I will be exalted upon the earth.

verses.context: Near the close of this psalm about disaster and refuge, God himself is quoted telling the nations to stop and take notice.

KJV.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
KJV.displayText: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

BSB.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
BSB.displayText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

CPDV.text: Create a clean heart in me, O God. And renew an upright spirit within my inmost being.
CPDV.displayText: Create a clean heart in me, O God. And renew an upright spirit within my inmost being.

verses.context: Written after the prophet Nathan confronted him over his affair with Bathsheba, David asks God for a fresh start.

KJV.text: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
KJV.displayText: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

BSB.text: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
BSB.displayText: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.

CPDV.text: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will nurture you. He will not allow the just to be tossed about forever.
CPDV.displayText: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will nurture you. He will not allow the just to be tossed about forever.

verses.context: Betrayed by a close friend, David tells himself in this psalm to hand his burden over to God and trust God to hold him up.

KJV.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
KJV.displayText: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

BSB.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
BSB.displayText: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.

CPDV.text: From the height of the day, I will be afraid. But truly, I will hope in you.
CPDV.displayText: From the height of the day, I will be afraid. But truly, I will hope in you.

verses.context: Written after the Philistines had captured him in the city of Gath, David admits his fear and where he takes it.

KJV.text: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
KJV.displayText: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?

BSB.text: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle— are they not in Your book?
BSB.displayText: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle— are they not in Your book?

CPDV.text: O God, I have announced my life to you. You have placed my tears in your sight, and even in your promise.
CPDV.displayText: O God, I have announced my life to you. You have placed my tears in your sight, and even in your promise.

verses.context: This same psalm, written while David was a captive, goes on to describe God keeping track of every tear he sheds.

KJV.text: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
KJV.displayText: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

BSB.text: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
BSB.displayText: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

CPDV.text: I cried out to you from the ends of the earth. When my heart was in anguish, you exalted me on a rock. You have led me,
CPDV.displayText: I cried out to you from the ends of the earth. When my heart was in anguish, you exalted me on a rock. You have led me,

verses.context: Praying from somewhere far from home, David asks to be led to a place of safety higher than himself.

KJV.text: Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocency.
KJV.displayText: Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocency.

BSB.text: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
BSB.displayText: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.

CPDV.text: And I said: So then, it is without purpose that I have justified my heart and washed my hands among the innocent.
CPDV.displayText: And I said: So then, it is without purpose that I have justified my heart and washed my hands among the innocent.

verses.context: Written by Asaph, a temple musician, this verse voices his doubt after watching wicked people prosper while he suffers.

KJV.text: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
KJV.displayText: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

BSB.text: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
BSB.displayText: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.

CPDV.text: My body has failed, and my heart: O God of my heart, and God my portion, into eternity.
CPDV.displayText: My body has failed, and my heart: O God of my heart, and God my portion, into eternity.

verses.context: By the end of this psalm, Asaph's body may be failing, but he describes God as his strength regardless.

KJV.text: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies? Selah.
KJV.displayText: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies?

BSB.text: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah
BSB.displayText: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?”

CPDV.text: And would God ever forget to be merciful? Or, would he, in his wrath, restrict his mercies?
CPDV.displayText: And would God ever forget to be merciful? Or, would he, in his wrath, restrict his mercies?

verses.context: Wrestling with doubt, Asaph asks aloud in this psalm whether God has simply stopped being merciful.

KJV.text: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
KJV.displayText: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.

BSB.text: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
BSB.displayText: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

CPDV.text: For one day in your courts is better than thousands elsewhere. I have chosen to be lowly in the house of my God, rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.
CPDV.displayText: For one day in your courts is better than thousands elsewhere. I have chosen to be lowly in the house of my God, rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.

verses.context: Longing simply to be near God's temple, the sons of Korah compare one day there to a thousand anywhere else.

KJV.text: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee.
KJV.displayText: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee.

BSB.text: For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.
BSB.displayText: For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.

CPDV.text: For you are sweet and mild, Lord, and plentiful in mercy to all who call upon you.
CPDV.displayText: For you are sweet and mild, Lord, and plentiful in mercy to all who call upon you.

verses.context: Calling himself poor and needy in this prayer, David describes God as quick to forgive and full of mercy.

KJV.text: Lord, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?
KJV.displayText: Lord, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?

BSB.text: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?
BSB.displayText: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?

CPDV.text: Lord, why do you reject my prayer? Why do you turn your face away from me?
CPDV.displayText: Lord, why do you reject my prayer? Why do you turn your face away from me?

verses.context: One of the darkest psalms, this one written by Heman, a temple musician, asks God directly why he feels abandoned.

KJV.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
KJV.displayText: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

BSB.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.
BSB.displayText: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.

CPDV.text: be numbered? So make known your right hand, along with men learned in heart, in wisdom.
CPDV.displayText: be numbered? So make known your right hand, along with men learned in heart, in wisdom.

verses.context: Reflecting on how short life is, the writer of this prayer attributed to Moses asks for wisdom about how to spend the time left.

KJV.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
KJV.displayText: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

BSB.text: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.
BSB.displayText: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.

CPDV.text: The Praise of a Canticle, of David. Whoever dwells with the assistance of the Most High will abide in the protection of the God of heaven.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever dwells with the assistance of the Most High will abide in the protection of the God of heaven.

verses.context: With no named author, this psalm opens by describing the safety of a person who stays close to God.

KJV.text: I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
KJV.displayText: I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.

BSB.text: I will say to the LORD, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
BSB.displayText: I will say to the LORD, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”

CPDV.text: He will say to the Lord, “You are my supporter and my refuge.” My God, I will hope in him.
CPDV.displayText: He will say to the Lord, “You are my supporter and my refuge.” My God, I will hope in him.

verses.context: A few lines into the same psalm, the writer responds with his own personal declaration of trust in God.

KJV.text: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
KJV.displayText: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.

BSB.text: He will cover you with His feathers; under His wings you will find refuge; His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.
BSB.displayText: He will cover you with His feathers; under His wings you will find refuge; His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.

CPDV.text: He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and you will hope under his wings.
CPDV.displayText: He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and you will hope under his wings.

verses.context: Using the image of a bird's sheltering feathers and wings, the same psalm describes God's protection as something close and constant.

KJV.text: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
KJV.displayText: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

BSB.text: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
BSB.displayText: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

CPDV.text: For he has given his Angels charge over you, so as to preserve you in all your ways.
CPDV.displayText: For he has given his Angels charge over you, so as to preserve you in all your ways.

verses.context: This verse from the same psalm is later quoted by the devil while tempting Jesus in the wilderness, according to the Gospels.

KJV.text: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.
KJV.displayText: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.

BSB.text: Let us enter His presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to Him in song.
BSB.displayText: Let us enter His presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to Him in song.

CPDV.text: Let us anticipate his presence with confession, and let us sing joyfully to him with psalms.
CPDV.displayText: Let us anticipate his presence with confession, and let us sing joyfully to him with psalms.

verses.context: Part of a call to worship with no named author, this verse invites the reader to come into God's presence giving thanks.

KJV.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
KJV.displayText: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.

BSB.text: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.
BSB.displayText: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.

CPDV.text: Enter his gates with confession, his courts with hymns, and acknowledge him. Praise his name.
CPDV.displayText: Enter his gates with confession, his courts with hymns, and acknowledge him. Praise his name.

verses.context: Labeled simply a psalm of praise with no named author, this verse instructs worshippers on how to enter the temple courts.

KJV.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
KJV.displayText: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:

BSB.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds—
BSB.displayText: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds—

CPDV.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his recompenses.
CPDV.displayText: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his recompenses.

verses.context: David tells his own soul not to forget anything good God has done for him, at the start of this psalm.

KJV.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.
KJV.displayText: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

BSB.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.
BSB.displayText: As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.

CPDV.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our iniquities from us.
CPDV.displayText: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our iniquities from us.

verses.context: A few verses on, David uses the distance between east and west to describe how completely God forgives.

KJV.text: O give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
KJV.displayText: O give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

BSB.text: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.
BSB.displayText: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.

CPDV.text: Alleluia. Confess to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is with every generation.
CPDV.displayText: Confess to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is with every generation.

verses.context: Opening a section of thanksgiving psalms with no named author, this verse calls on the reader to give thanks because God is good.

KJV.text: What shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me?
KJV.displayText: What shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me?

BSB.text: How can I repay the LORD for all His goodness to me?
BSB.displayText: How can I repay the LORD for all His goodness to me?

CPDV.text: What shall I repay to the Lord, for all the things that he has repaid to me?
CPDV.displayText: What shall I repay to the Lord, for all the things that he has repaid to me?

verses.context: With no author named, the writer of this psalm asks what he can possibly give back to God for all he has received.

KJV.text: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
KJV.displayText: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

BSB.text: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints.
BSB.displayText: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints.

CPDV.text: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones.
CPDV.displayText: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones.

verses.context: This thanksgiving psalm goes on to say that God values the lives of his faithful people even in their death.

KJV.text: This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
KJV.displayText: This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

BSB.text: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

BSB.text: How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!
BSB.displayText: How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!

CPDV.text: But to me, O God, your friends have been greatly honored. Their first ruler has been exceedingly strengthened.
CPDV.displayText: But to me, O God, your friends have been greatly honored. Their first ruler has been exceedingly strengthened.

verses.context: In a psalm marveling at how completely God knows him, David says God's thoughts toward him outnumber anything he could count.

KJV.text: I looked on my right hand, and beheld, but there was no man that would know me: refuge failed me; no man cared for my soul.
KJV.displayText: I looked on my right hand, and beheld, but there was no man that would know me: refuge failed me; no man cared for my soul.

BSB.text: Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul.
BSB.displayText: Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul.

CPDV.text: I considered toward the right, and I looked, but there was no one who would know me. Flight has perished before me, and there is no one who has concern for my soul.
CPDV.displayText: I considered toward the right, and I looked, but there was no one who would know me. Flight has perished before me, and there is no one who has concern for my soul.

verses.context: Hiding in a cave from Saul, David writes this psalm admitting that no one nearby seems to notice him or care for his safety.

KJV.text: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.
KJV.displayText: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.

BSB.text: Let me hear Your loving devotion in the morning, for I have put my trust in You. Teach me the way I should walk, for to You I lift up my soul.
BSB.displayText: Let me hear Your loving devotion in the morning, for I have put my trust in You. Teach me the way I should walk, for to You I lift up my soul.

CPDV.text: Make me hear your mercy in the morning. For I have hoped in you. Make known to me the way that I should walk. For I have lifted up my soul to you.
CPDV.displayText: Make me hear your mercy in the morning. For I have hoped in you. Make known to me the way that I should walk. For I have lifted up my soul to you.

verses.context: Early in this prayer during a time of distress, David asks God to let him hear of his love each morning and show him which way to walk.

KJV.text: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.
KJV.displayText: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.

BSB.text: The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down.
BSB.displayText: The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down.

CPDV.text: The Lord lifts up all who have fallen down, and he sets upright all who have been thrown down.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord lifts up all who have fallen down, and he sets upright all who have been thrown down.

verses.context: In this praise psalm, David points out that God notices the weak and struggling, not only the strong and successful.

KJV.text: He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.
KJV.displayText: He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.

BSB.text: He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name.
BSB.displayText: He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name.

CPDV.text: He numbers the multitude of the stars, and he calls them all by their names.
CPDV.displayText: He numbers the multitude of the stars, and he calls them all by their names.

verses.context: Celebrating Jerusalem's restoration in this psalm, the writer marvels that the same God who heals broken hearts also names every star.

KJV.text: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
KJV.displayText: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

BSB.text: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.
BSB.displayText: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.

CPDV.text: Go to the ant, you lazy one, and consider her ways, and so learn wisdom.
CPDV.displayText: Go to the ant, you lazy one, and consider her ways, and so learn wisdom.

verses.context: Addressing a sluggard directly, Solomon points him to the ant, urging him to learn diligence by watching how it works.

KJV.text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
KJV.displayText: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

BSB.text: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
BSB.displayText: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.

CPDV.text: Whoever walks dishonestly reveals secrets. But whoever is of a faithful soul conceals what is confided by a friend.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever walks dishonestly reveals secrets. But whoever is of a faithful soul conceals what is confided by a friend.

verses.context: Solomon warns his son in this proverb that a gossip spreads secrets, while someone trustworthy keeps a confidence.

KJV.text: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.
KJV.displayText: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.

BSB.text: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
BSB.displayText: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

CPDV.text: For this reason, accept one another, just as Christ also has accepted you, in the honor of God.
CPDV.displayText: For this reason, accept one another, just as Christ also has accepted you, in the honor of God.

verses.context: Near the end of a section on unity, Paul tells the Roman church to welcome each other the same way Christ welcomed them.

KJV.text: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
KJV.displayText: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

BSB.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
BSB.displayText: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

CPDV.text: Whoever keeps step with the wise shall be wise. A friend of the foolish will become like them.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever keeps step with the wise shall be wise. A friend of the foolish will become like them.

verses.context: Solomon tells his son in this proverb that the company he keeps, wise or foolish, will end up shaping who he becomes.

KJV.text: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
KJV.displayText: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

BSB.text: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.
BSB.displayText: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.

CPDV.text: Whoever follows justice and mercy shall discover life, justice, and glory.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever follows justice and mercy shall discover life, justice, and glory.

verses.context: In this collection of Solomon's own proverbs, chasing after goodness and mercy is said to bring life and honor.

KJV.text: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
KJV.displayText: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

BSB.text: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
BSB.displayText: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.

CPDV.text: Intentions dissipate where there is no counsel. Yet truly, they are confirmed where there are many counselors.
CPDV.displayText: Intentions dissipate where there is no counsel. Yet truly, they are confirmed where there are many counselors.

verses.context: Among his practical sayings, Solomon observes that plans collapse without advice, but succeed once many advisers weigh in.

KJV.text: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
KJV.displayText: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

BSB.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
BSB.displayText: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

CPDV.text: Careful words are a honeycomb: sweet to the soul and healthful to the bones.
CPDV.displayText: Careful words are a honeycomb: sweet to the soul and healthful to the bones.

verses.context: Teaching his son about the power of words, Solomon compares kind speech to honey, sweet to the taste and good for the body.

KJV.text: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
KJV.displayText: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

BSB.text: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
BSB.displayText: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

CPDV.text: A patient man is better than a strong one. And whoever rules his soul is better than one who assaults cities.
CPDV.displayText: A patient man is better than a strong one. And whoever rules his soul is better than one who assaults cities.

verses.context: Teaching his son the value of self-control, Solomon says mastering your own temper matters more than any military victory.

KJV.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
KJV.displayText: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

BSB.text: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
BSB.displayText: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

CPDV.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue. Whoever values it shall eat from its fruits.
CPDV.displayText: Death and life are in the power of the tongue. Whoever values it shall eat from its fruits.

verses.context: Solomon warns his son here that words carry real power, able to give life or bring harm, with the effects landing back on the speaker.

KJV.text: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.
KJV.displayText: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.

BSB.displayText: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.

CPDV.text: Because of this, setting aside lying, speak the truth, each one with his neighbor. For we are all part of one another.
CPDV.displayText: Because of this, setting aside lying, speak the truth, each one with his neighbor. For we are all part of one another.

verses.context: Instructing the Ephesian church on their new way of life, Paul tells them to stop lying and speak truthfully to each other instead.

KJV.text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
KJV.displayText: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

BSB.text: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
BSB.displayText: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.

CPDV.text: Whoever is merciful to the poor lends to the Lord. And he will repay him for his efforts.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever is merciful to the poor lends to the Lord. And he will repay him for his efforts.

verses.context: Solomon tells his son that showing kindness to the poor is like making a loan directly to the Lord, who repays it in full.

KJV.text: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.
KJV.displayText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.

BSB.text: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
BSB.displayText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

CPDV.text: It is a luxurious thing, wine, and inebriation is tumultuous. Anyone who is delighted by this will not be wise.
CPDV.displayText: It is a luxurious thing, wine, and inebriation is tumultuous. Anyone who is delighted by this will not be wise.

verses.context: Warning his son about habits that ruin good judgment, Solomon cautions him against being led astray by strong drink.

KJV.text: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
KJV.displayText: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.

BSB.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
BSB.displayText: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.

CPDV.text: A good name is better than many riches. And good esteem is above silver and gold.
CPDV.displayText: A good name is better than many riches. And good esteem is above silver and gold.

verses.context: Teaching his son what to value most in life, Solomon ranks a trustworthy reputation above any amount of money.

KJV.text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
KJV.displayText: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

BSB.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
BSB.displayText: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

CPDV.text: If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
CPDV.displayText: If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

verses.context: Teaching his son how to treat an enemy, Solomon instructs him to feed a hungry rival and give a thirsty one water.

KJV.text: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
KJV.displayText: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

BSB.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
BSB.displayText: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.

CPDV.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what the future day may bring.
CPDV.displayText: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what the future day may bring.

verses.context: Solomon cautions his son against boasting about tomorrow, since no one actually knows what a single day will bring.

KJV.text: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.
KJV.displayText: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.

BSB.text: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.
BSB.displayText: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.

CPDV.displayText: Ointment and various perfumes delight the heart. And the good advice of a friend is sweet to the soul.

verses.context: Teaching his son what good friendship looks like, Solomon commends a friend's heartfelt advice as one of life's true pleasures.

KJV.text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
KJV.displayText: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

BSB.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
BSB.displayText: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

CPDV.displayText: The impious flees, though no one pursues. But the just, like a confident lion, shall be without dread.

verses.context: In a section contrasting the wicked and the righteous, Solomon tells his son how a guilty conscience can make a person fearful.

KJV.text: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
KJV.displayText: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.

BSB.text: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
BSB.displayText: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.

CPDV.text: In every work, there shall be abundance. But where there are many words, there is often need.
CPDV.displayText: In every work, there shall be abundance. But where there are many words, there is often need.

verses.context: Solomon tells his son that steady work pays off, while talk that never becomes action leads only to want.

KJV.text: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
KJV.displayText: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

BSB.text: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
BSB.displayText: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.

CPDV.displayText: Strength and elegance are her clothing, and she will laugh in the final days.

verses.context: Near the end of a poem taught to King Lemuel by his mother, a capable wife is pictured clothed in strength and unafraid of the future.

KJV.text: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
KJV.displayText: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

BSB.text: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
BSB.displayText: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.

CPDV.displayText: “A handful with rest is better than both hands filled with labors and with affliction of the soul.”

verses.context: The Preacher, still reflecting on the emptiness of nonstop striving, concludes that a little peace beats a lot gained through constant struggle.

KJV.text: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
KJV.displayText: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.

BSB.text: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
BSB.displayText: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

CPDV.text: The end of a speech is better than the beginning. Patience is better than arrogance.
CPDV.displayText: The end of a speech is better than the beginning. Patience is better than arrogance.

verses.context: In this list of short proverb-like sayings, the Preacher contrasts a patient, humble attitude with the impulsive pride he warns against throughout the book.

KJV.text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
KJV.displayText: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

BSB.text: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
BSB.displayText: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

CPDV.displayText: I turned myself toward another thing, and I saw that under the sun, the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to the learned, nor grace to the skillful: but there is a time and an end for all these things.

verses.context: Observing how life actually plays out, the Preacher notices that the fastest runner or strongest fighter doesn't always win, since chance plays a part too.

KJV.text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
KJV.displayText: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

BSB.displayText: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

CPDV.displayText: Cast your bread over running waters. For, after a long time, you shall find it again.

verses.context: Near the end of the book, the Preacher urges generosity, picturing it as bread cast on the water that eventually comes back.

KJV.text: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.
KJV.displayText: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.

BSB.displayText: I will rejoice greatly in the LORD, my soul will exult in my God; for He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

CPDV.text: I will rejoice greatly in the Lord, and my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with the vestments of salvation, and he has wrapped me in the clothing of justice, like a groom arrayed with a crown, and like a bride adorned with her jewels.
CPDV.displayText: I will rejoice greatly in the Lord, and my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with the vestments of salvation, and he has wrapped me in the clothing of justice, like a groom arrayed with a crown, and like a bride adorned with her jewels.

verses.context: In a passage of celebration, the speaker in Isaiah rejoices like a bride and groom dressed for their wedding, clothed by God himself.

KJV.text: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.
KJV.displayText: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.

BSB.text: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.
BSB.displayText: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.

CPDV.displayText: And the work of justice will be peace. And the service of justice will be quiet and secure, forever.

verses.context: Describing a future age of restoration for a devastated land, Isaiah connects the nation's righteousness directly to its lasting peace and safety.

KJV.displayText: And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

BSB.displayText: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.

CPDV.displayText: And the redeemed of the Lord will be converted, and they will return to Zion with praising. And everlasting joy will be upon their heads. They will obtain gladness and rejoicing. For pain and sorrow will flee away.

KJV.displayText: A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.

BSB.displayText: A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish; He will faithfully bring forth justice.

CPDV.displayText: The bruised reed he will not break, and the smoldering wick he will not extinguish. He will lead forth judgment unto truth.

KJV.displayText: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.

BSB.displayText: Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.

CPDV.displayText: All ends of the earth, be converted to me, and you will be saved. For I am God, and there is no other.

BSB.displayText: “Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you without money, come, buy, and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!

BSB.displayText: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.

CPDV.displayText: Remove, far from me, vanity and lying words. Give me neither begging, nor wealth. Apportion to me only the necessities of my life,

BSB.text: And I heard a voice from heaven telling me to write, “Blessed are the dead—those who die in the Lord from this moment on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.”

CPDV.text: And I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me: “Write: Blessed are the dead, who die in the Lord, now and hereafter, says the Spirit, so that they may find rest from their labors. For their works follow them.”
CPDV.displayText: And I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me: “Write: Blessed are the dead, who die in the Lord, now and hereafter, says the Spirit, so that they may find rest from their labors. For their works follow them.”

verses.context: In a vision late in Revelation, John hears a voice from heaven pronouncing a blessing on those who die trusting in the Lord, since their labors are finally over.

KJV.text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
KJV.displayText: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:

BSB.text: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
BSB.displayText: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,

CPDV.text: When your enemy will fall, do not be glad, and do not let your heart exult in his ruin,
CPDV.displayText: When your enemy will fall, do not be glad, and do not let your heart exult in his ruin,

verses.context: Part of a collection of wise sayings rather than Solomon's own proverbs, this verse cautions the reader against gloating when an enemy falls.
